name: Easy Pork and 3-Bean Chili

ingredients.name: boneless pork shoulder, trimmed and cut into 2-inch dice
whole tomatoes packed in juice, roughly squeezed through fingers to chop
red kidney beans, drained and rinsed

instructions.primary_message: Combine 1 cup chicken broth and raisins in a microwave-safe bowl and microwave on high heat until very hot, about 1 minute. Let stand for 5 minutes, then puree raisins and stock until smooth in a countertop blender or with an immersion blender. Add remaining cup of chicken stock and set aside.

Carefully pat pork dry with paper towels or a clean kitchen towel. Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed Dutch oven over high heat until smoking. Add pork all at once and spread evenly over bottom surface (it's ok if not all the pork is touching the bottom or if the pan is crowded). Cook without moving until bottom surface is well browned, about 8 minutes. Stir pork. Add onions and garlic and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes. Add oregano, chili powder, cumin, and coriander and cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant and a light patina forms on the bottom of the pan, about 3 minutes.

Add broth/rasin mixture, stirring to release browned bits from bottom of pan. Add tomatoes and their juice, fish sauce, orange juice concentrate (or orange juice) and bay leaf. Season lightly with salt and pepper and bring to a boil.
Reduce to a bare simmer, cover pot leaving lid slightly ajar, and cook, stirring occasionally, until pork is nearly tender, about 1 1/2 hours.

Add kidney beans, black beans, and garbanzo or cannellini beans. Continue to cook until pork can be easily shredded with a fork, about 45 minutes longer. Sauce should be thick, with an almost ketchup-like consistency. If too thin, continue to cook, stirring frequently, until reduced to the desired consistency. Season to taste with salt.
Serve chili with diced avocado, cilantro, diced onions, lime wedges, and grated cheese. Chili can be stored in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 5 days.

schema_metadata.keywords: black beans, cannellini beans, chili, garbanzo beans, kidney beans, pork, soup, The Food Lab

description: An easy 1-pot pork and three-bean chili with a rich, balanced chili flavor.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Diced avocado, cilantro, diced onions, lime wedges, and grated cheese for serving (optional)

Optional substitutions: low-sodium chicken broth → stock; vegetable oil → canola oil; garbanzo beans → cannellini beans
author: J. Kenji López-Alt
